slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The Data Landscapers 54-country review (an AI-assisted compilation, the author's own analysis) states that it found no evidence of direct digital recording of attendance, enrolment or grades at rural primary schools in Egypt, calls recording 'likely paper-based' with later aggregation, and scores schools 2 (predominantly paper with some digital or pilots); it gives no date, so the document's published date is used.

note: The paper statement is hedged in the document ('likely', 'no evidence'). The EMIS is left unclassified: the document names EMIS-linked daily attendance monitoring but says nothing of what schools enter, and reports an attendance rate above 80%, not a share of schools.

note: No fact: the author, an adviser to the minister, says EMIS-linked daily attendance monitoring was introduced and attendance rose above 80% nationwide by the end of 2024/25, with weekly attendance dashboards, but does not say that schools enter a record per learner, who enters it, at which levels or in how many schools; the EMIS is therefore left unclassified. If the parent reads daily attendance monitoring as entry during the year, this is the document that carries it.

facts.fact: The Education Sector Plan 2023-2027, the ministry's costed plan, says the 'traditional EMIS' of routine administrative tasks and student head counts will be expanded into a real-time, integrated EMIS ecosystem with data down to class and student level, decentralised digital data entry, a digital profile of each student and a link to the national ID, and gives 'strengthen EMIS' a programme and an expenditure line in each subsector including primary; no date is given for the statement, so the document's published date is used.

The Education Sector Plan 2023-2027 lists EMIS as a department of the Ministry of Education and Technical Education and makes the ministry responsible for building the planned integrated EMIS ecosystem; no date is given, so the document's published date is used.

facts.fact: The ministry said the platform will start in several education departments in 2026/2027 before gradual national expansion; no school count is given.
The platform is to give teachers digital tools to record attendance and absences and to monitor each student's performance and assessment results, with the ministry receiving updated data daily.

The education ministry signed an agreement with the Japanese company SPRIX on 10 August 2026 (announced that day) for a nationwide attendance, performance and assessment platform, starting in 2026/2027.
The Ministry of Education and Technical Education signed the agreement and says the platform is part of its integrated national digital system for managing and monitoring education.
